subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkyl, allylic, benzylic, vinylic and aryl halides
title: Alkyl, Vinyl, Allyl and Aryl Halides: Which Carbon Holds X?
summary: Alkyl, vinyl (vinylic), allyl (allylic) and aryl halides differ only in the carbon that holds the halogen. Alkyl: a saturated sp³ carbon (1°, 2°, 3° by the alkyl groups on it). Vinyl: X directly on a carbon of a C=C (sp²). Allyl: X on the sp³ carbon next to a C=C. Aryl: X directly on a carbon of an aromatic ring (sp²), e.g. chlorobenzene. Bonus: X on the sp³ CH₂ next to a benzene ring is a benzyl (benzylic) halide. Identify the carbon attached to X: that's the key.

notes.title: 03 – Alkyl, Vinyl, Allyl and Aryl Halides

keyPoints: **Three steps**: find the carbon bonded to X → is it **sp³ or sp²**? → what is **next door**?
**sp³ C–X**: **alkyl** (R–X; 1°, 2°, 3° by alkyl groups on that carbon), **allylic** (next to a C=C, e.g. CH₂=CHCH₂Cl) and **benzylic** (attached to a benzene ring, e.g. C₆H₅CH₂Cl).
**sp² C–X**: **vinylic** (X on the C=C carbon, e.g. CH₂=CHCl) and **aryl** (X directly on a ring carbon, e.g. C₆H₅Cl, a haloarene).
**The trap**: a C=C in the molecule does not make it vinylic; X one carbon away from the C=C is **allylic**. X on the CH₂ outside a ring is **benzylic**, not aryl.
**Why it matters**: benzyl chloride gives benzyl alcohol with NaOH(aq) easily; chlorobenzene needs **623 K and 300 atm**, because its sp² C–Cl bond is shorter and stronger.

blocks.p: **JEE Main 2024 (27 January, Shift 2).** Which among the following halide(s) will not show SN1 reaction?

**Answer: (B).** Classify first. (A) Cl is on the sp³ carbon next to the C=C: allylic. (C) Cl is on the sp³ CH₂ attached to the ring: benzylic. (D) secondary alkyl. (B) Cl sits on a C=C carbon: **vinylic**, an sp² C–Cl. Losing Cl⁻ would leave the positive charge on an sp² carbon (a vinyl cation), which is very unstable, and the sp² C–Cl bond is also stronger; so (B) does not undergo SN1. Allylic and benzylic cations are stabilised by resonance and the 2° cation by alkyl groups, so (A), (C) and (D) can.

quiz.q: Halides are classified as alkyl, allylic, benzylic, vinylic or aryl by looking at:
options: the hybridisation and neighbour of the carbon bonded to X
the length of the carbon chain
quiz.explain: NCERT 6.1.2–6.1.3: the carbon bonded to X decides the class.
Cl is on the sp³ CH₂ next to the C=C.
Cl sits on a C=C carbon (sp²).
Cl is on the sp³ CH₂ attached to the ring.
Cl is directly on a ring carbon (sp²).

quiz.q: In which pair is the carbon bonded to X sp2 in both?
quiz.explain: Both have X on an sp² carbon.
Three alkyl groups on the carbon holding Cl.

quiz.q: Chlorobenzene gives phenol with aqueous NaOH only at:
Why is the C–Cl bond of chlorobenzene harder to break than that of benzyl chloride?
options: the carbon bonded to Cl is sp2, so the bond is shorter and stronger
quiz.explain: More s-character: shorter, stronger C–Cl bond.
Cl on the sp³ carbon attached to the ring; two alkyl/aryl groups: 2° benzylic.
